root_idea.summary: The root centers on continued movement or release: something runs onward, goes away, or is set free.
root_idea.development: The movement principle extends to releasing an animal or person, and metaphorically to a gift as something made to flow. Minerals or buried treasure are understood as a divinely flowing gift, while the word for unripe dates is treated as a divergent branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized feminine active-participle citation form سَائِبَةٌ.

senses.definition: A consecrated animal released to pasture at will, especially the she-camel set free under a pre-Islamic vow or custom and exempted from riding.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic usage, the term denotes the pagan animal custom. Classical usage can describe more generally a beast left to pasture without a herder; the separate Classical use for an emancipated slave is not intended here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run or flow, especially of water; to run of itself.
To move along quickly or in a continuous course; of a snake, to go into or emerge from its lair, and of a person or thing, to go or return toward a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A movement sense extending beyond the specific flow of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go at random or in every direction; of an animal, to range or pasture freely without a keeper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of horses, beasts, and similar subjects allowed to go where they will.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rove or ramble in speech; to speak diffusely, profusely, or without restraint.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage referring to loose or irrational discourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave a thing alone, abandon it, or neglect it.
To let an animal pasture wherever it will, without a keeper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a beast or she-camel deliberately left free to range.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An emancipated slave whose former owner has no claim to inherit from him or control his property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate legal and social use of the feminine noun, distinct from the Quranic animal term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal given up or dedicated to God, including an animal designated as an offering because it has been surrendered to Him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional religious usage attested for animals presented as offerings; it is distinct from the specific Quranic pagan pasture custom.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gift, benefaction, voluntary alms, favour, or benefit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be used for an act of generosity or a benefit that flows abundantly to its recipients.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A flowing or beneficial fall of rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized interpretation in a prayer for rain, where the word may denote rain as a beneficial flow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Metal, mineral wealth, or buried treasure extracted or found in the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural form used for ore, veins of gold or silver, or pre-Islamic buried treasure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hair of a horse’s tail.
A pole used to propel a ship or boat.
A place or channel in which water runs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal term for a watercourse or channel.
An Arabicized Persian noun and a separate lexical item from the native root branches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unripe or green dates, especially dates in the balah or busr stage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular is سَيَابَةٌ or related dialectal variants; this branch is treated as divergent from the root’s central movement sense.
A masculine active-participial noun used substantivally for flowing water.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Form IV horse usage is equated with رَفَّضَ, but the referenced semantic explanation is not supplied.
Pointer directing the reader back to Form I.
Infinitive identification and cross-reference, with no independent lexical branch.
Pointer to the entry for سَيَابٌ.

cautions: Classical accounts differ over the exact vow or circumstance associated with the pre-Islamic sāʾibah custom; the Quranic core is an animal released and consecrated in that practice.
The Form IV horse usage remains unresolved because the packet supplies only an equation with رَفَّضَ and no semantic gloss for that referenced entry.
